points: Q3 2026 is the first live quarter after reports of a strong Q2 2026 print and a full-year guidance raise, so the Oct 28 release will test whether summer traffic, off-premise sales and dine-in momentum carried through September.

The 90-day revenue estimate is up 1.96% with 5 upward revisions and zero down over the past 30 days; the print will show whether analysts are still underestimating demand or have already priced in the recovery.

FY1 EPS of $2.37 implies only 4.8% growth while FY2 EPS of $2.73 implies 15.4% growth; Q3 results and guidance will reveal whether that second-year earnings acceleration is backed by real operations or just consensus math.

BJRI trades at a P/E roughly in line with the restaurant median but a PEG about 3.1x the median, so the print needs to show operating leverage—through pricing, labor efficiency or food-cost control—to justify the premium valuation on a long.
Management’s updated full-year guidance is the key read; reaffirming or lifting FY1 EPS toward $2.37 and giving a constructive Q4/holiday outlook would support the long case.

New-unit progress and regional performance, especially outside California, will show whether growth is more than a comp recovery; any acceleration in development or sustained strength in Texas/Florida/Ohio supports the path to FY2 $2.73.
BROS reports Nov 5 and may offer a peer read-through on traffic and pricing, but BJRI’s own Q3 execution and guidance are the primary drivers of the trade.
watch: Comparable restaurant sales trend: sequential improvement or sustained positive momentum supports the long.
Weekly sales per restaurant: continued upward trend supports the long.
Full-year EPS guidance: raised or reaffirmed near $2.37 supports the long.
Restaurant-level margin and cost commentary: expansion or stable outlook supports the long.
